title.narrative: Tradin Organic Agriculture: Valorising the mango value chain in The Gambia

description.narrative: 5 to 10 years ago, the government of fragile state The Gambia heavily promoted the cultivation of mangos which has led to the current abundance of mangos and price droppings. A lack of market access opportunities, combined with inefficiencies in the mango chain, has resulted in extremely high crop losses for farmers during the short (4 months) mango season, challenging their livelihoods.Tradin is currently one of the world’s biggest suppliers of organic dried mango which are imported from West Africa (amongst others). In order to meet world-wide growing demand for dried mangos, the company aimed to develop an organic dried mango value chain and increase production in The Gambia by investing in its young local partner Tropingo Foods. Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) is used to invest in the set-up of an organic supply chain, additional equipment and drying facilities, improvement of quality- and operational processes within the facility and a feasibility study for a large scale factory and mango plantation. The project is the first to process mango and the first ‘organic’ project in the country. It supported 200+ direct jobs (80 FTE) and 256 indirect jobs of smallholder farmers in the supply chain. Both, the employees in the processing facility as the mango farmers, received training on good manufacturing practices and good agricultural practices, including organic production and these farmers are now cultivating according to international organic standards leading to new income streams. As a result of the Technical Assistance, the factory is now an approved vendor and certified supplier of dried mangos. Further investments are currently being explored and may result in the creation of more than 500 new jobs in the next few years.
